contentFull:
Smart innovations, S. suis and sustainability in Pig Progress 3 

The latest edition of Pig Progress is now available online. From Vietnam’s move towards large-scale pig production and the latest innovations at EuroTier 2026 to Denmark’s progress in tackling PRRS and the future of pig genetics, this edition explores the developments shaping the global pig industry. This and much more in the latest edition of Pig Progress.

Natalie KinsleyFreelance journalist

Oct 16

News

Read this edition of Pig Progress here!Rebuilding Vietnam’s pig industry with a little help from China

Vietnam’s pork industry is undergoing an enormous transformation. Since the emergence of ASF, backyard producers have been rapidly replaced by large-scale pig projects. Biosecurity, sustainability and precision technology are increasingly shaping the sector. With some help from China, Vietnam’s BAF Agriculture is taking pig farming – literally – to the next level. Pages 6-12.

What innovations are in the spotlight at EuroTier 2026?

More than ever before, swine innovations are advancing at an incredible pace. Artificial intelligence (AI), in particular, is creating new opportunities and practical applications in the pig house. It is no surprise, then, that AI and other promising innovations will be in the spotlight at EuroTier 2026 in Hanover, Germany. In total, 13 innovations were awarded medals: 2 gold and 11 silver. Here’s what to look out for. Pages 16-19.

The Smart Farrowing Pen by Weda received one of the four gold medals in EuroTier 2026. Photo: Weda

Interview: Control of S. suis is essential for further reduction of antibiotics

Reducing antibiotic use is a priority in many countries. But when are antibiotics still needed? One common reason is to control Streptococcus suis infections in pigs. This could change in the near future, as a cross-protective vaccine is expected to be launched soon, says Prof Dr Christoph Baums of Leipzig University, Germany. Pages 24-26.

Column: Sustainable and circular feed

In this column, Francesc Molist explores how circular by-products and liquid feeding can reduce feed’s carbon footprint, while balancing costs, circularity and nutrient efficiency. Page 27.

Farm visit: No more transports, but producing own piglets

Six finisher pig producers joined forces to build a modern sow house in north-western Romania. A subsidy of €8.1 million from Romania’s Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development helped turn their vision into reality. Pages 28-31.

Years of dreaming, planning, considering, talking and taking action was needed for the realisation of a modern sow facility for 1,921 sows in Romania. Photo: Mark Pasveer

How Denmark has rapidly tackled its PRRS problem

After 5 years, Denmark’s PRRS reduction plan is showing results, with three-quarters of farms now virus-free. Transparency and a regional approach have been key to progress in tackling the disease. In Denmark, PRRS-free status means pigs have no antibodies against either the vaccine virus or the field virus. Pages 34-36.

Farm visit: Yeast and stockmanship lift up farm performance

Good stockmanship is essential for a successful pig farm. Combined with the effective use of prebiotics and probiotics, it can deliver surprising results. At Albæk Agro in Denmark, improved farm efficiency even led to a reduction in the number of sows. Pages 40-43.

Interview: Huge amounts of data determine the future of pig genetics – here’s why

Artificial intelligence (AI) is set to play an increasingly important role in accelerating genetic progress, particularly for breeding companies. As swine genetics company Axiom celebrates its 10th anniversary, CEO Guillaume Naveau reflects on the company’s journey and looks ahead to the future. Pages 46-47.

A “glocal” focus – how a new meat giant strives to reach its markets

The MBRF Innovation Centre in São Paulo state, Brazil. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

In 2025, Brazilian meat companies Marfrig and BRF joined forces to form MBRF, a major player with products reaching 117 markets worldwide. How does the company manage such a vast global network and meet the needs of customers around the world? Pages 51-53.

Global trade in pork never stands still

Animal diseases, import tariffs and legislative changes all shape global pork trade. A recent long-term analysis by Rabobank highlights the major impact of African Swine Fever (ASF) on trade flows, while also revealing surprising developments in the Americas. Pages 55-58.

Column: Delaying euthanasia

In this column by animal scientist Laya Kannan S. Alves, the importance of timely euthanasia in pig production is explored, highlighting how clear protocols can reduce animal suffering, support caretakers and avoid unnecessary costs. Page 62.

translationZh:
**最新一期Pig Progress现已上线**

从越南迈向规模化养猪生产、EuroTier 2026的最新创新，到丹麦在应对PRRS方面的进展以及猪遗传育种的未来，本期探讨塑造全球养猪业发展的诸多动态。更多内容尽在本期Pig Progress。

**借助中国之力重建越南养猪业**

越南养猪业正在经历巨大转型。自非洲猪瘟（ASF）出现以来，后院养殖户正迅速被大型养猪项目取代。生物安全、可持续性和精准技术日益塑造着该行业。在中国的帮助下，越南BAF农业公司正将养猪业——名副其实地——提升到新的水平。第6-12页。

**EuroTier 2026有哪些创新成为焦点？**

猪业创新的推进速度前所未有。尤其是人工智能（AI），正在猪舍中创造新的机遇和实际应用。因此，AI及其他有前景的创新成为在德国汉诺威举行的EuroTier 2026的焦点并不令人意外。共有13项创新获得奖牌：2项金奖和11项银奖。以下是值得关注的内容。第16-19页。

**专访：控制猪链球菌对进一步减少抗生素至关重要**

减少抗生素使用是许多国家的优先事项。但何时仍然需要抗生素？一个常见原因是控制猪的猪链球菌感染。德国莱比锡大学Christoph Baums教授表示，随着一种跨保护疫苗有望很快上市，这种情况可能在不久的将来发生改变。第24-26页。

**专栏：可持续与循环饲料**

在本专栏中，Francesc Molist探讨循环副产品和液态饲喂如何降低饲料的碳足迹，同时平衡成本、循环性和营养效率。第27页。

**农场访问：不再运输，而是自产仔猪**

六名育肥猪生产者联合在罗马尼亚西北部建造了一座现代化母猪舍。罗马尼亚农业与农村发展部提供的810万欧元补贴帮助他们的愿景成为现实。第28-31页。

**丹麦如何迅速解决其PRRS问题**

五年后，丹麦的PRRS减少计划正在显现成效，四分之三的农场现已无病毒。透明度和区域化方法是取得进展的关键。在丹麦，PRRS无疫状态意味着猪只对疫苗病毒和野毒均无抗体。第34-36页。

**农场访问：酵母与饲养管理提升农场绩效**

良好的饲养管理对成功的养猪场至关重要。结合有效使用益生元和益生菌，可以带来令人惊喜的成果。在丹麦Albæk Agro，农场效率的提升甚至导致了母猪数量的减少。第40-43页。

**专访：海量数据决定猪遗传育种的未来——原因如下**

人工智能（AI）将在加速遗传进展方面发挥越来越重要的作用，尤其是对育种公司而言。在猪遗传育种公司Axiom庆祝成立10周年之际，CEO Guillaume Naveau回顾了公司的发展历程并展望未来。第46-47页。

**“全球本土化”聚焦——一家新肉类巨头如何触达其市场**

2025年，巴西肉类公司Marfrig和BRF联手组建MBRF，成为产品覆盖全球117个市场的主要参与者。该公司如何管理如此庞大的全球网络并满足世界各地客户的需求？第51-53页。

**全球猪肉贸易从未停滞**

动物疾病、进口关税和立法变化都在塑造全球猪肉贸易。荷兰合作银行（Rabobank）最近的一项长期分析强调了非洲猪瘟（ASF）对贸易流的重大影响，同时揭示了美洲令人惊讶的发展动态。第55-58页。

**专栏：推迟安乐死**

在动物科学家Laya Kannan S. Alves的专栏中，探讨了养猪生产中及时实施安乐死的重要性，强调明确的规程如何减少动物痛苦、支持饲养员并避免不必要的成本。第62页。
author: Natalie Kinsley
